about.headline: I like making complicated software feel obvious.
about.intro:
I'm a Product Designer at Microsoft on Office Shared Experiences, where I work on Catch Up in Word and Copilot. Before that, I worked on AI experiences and automation, and on Microsoft Stream.

I studied at Purdue and co-founded benefit.design, a nonprofit that connects student volunteer designers with nonprofits that need design help.

These days, a lot of my thinking happens in code. I prototype with Claude to test ideas quickly, and I bring that speed back into design work.

how.title: Grounded in research
how.text: I start with what people are actually trying to get done. I've run 200+ interviews and usability tests, and I let what I hear decide what to build, including whether AI should be involved at all.

how.title: Ethics and accessibility from the start
how.text: I treat both as design inputs, not a final check. I've led accessibility research with people with disabilities and written accessibility specs, and I've contributed to published research on ethics in UX practice. For AI features, that means clear attribution, honest feedback, and an easy way to undo.

how.title: Prototyping to communicate and experiment
how.text: A working prototype settles questions a static screen can't. I use prototypes to test ideas quickly and to help a team and leaders see the same thing, as with the agentic Gather vision prototype. I build them in Figma and, increasingly, by vibe coding working versions with Claude.

experience.text: Six years designing AI-powered collaboration across Word, Copilot Chat, and Teams. **Catch Up:** took a Copilot Chat skill from concept to release and set the UX vision for catching up across Word. **Gather:** led V1 in Copilot Actions end to end, then built the agentic vision prototype that earned executive sponsorship and shaped a strategic pivot. **Stream:** redesigned screen recording (+9.9% start-to-upload completion in early data) and led accessibility research with 27 interviews.
Started a nonprofit that matches student volunteer designers with nonprofits that need design support.

experience.role: UX Design, BS. Minors in Psychology and Management
experience.text: Where I got my start. Alongside classes, I interned at Pivotal Cloud Foundry, Zero Systems, and Microsoft, worked as an undergraduate research assistant on dark patterns (UXP2 Lab) and on a course website (Freeform), and was Secretary of Purdue UX and on the media team for Purdue Hackers.

about.outside:
Outside of work, you'll usually find me outdoors, or planning my next trip. Travel is how I reset and stay curious. I love getting to a new place, wandering without too strict a plan, and coming home with a head full of stories. National parks are my favorite version of that: a good trail, a big view, and the feeling of being very small in a very beautiful place.

I'm also happiest when I'm training for something. Endurance sports give me a goal on the calendar, a reason to get up early, and a steady kind of progress I find really satisfying. Fitness has become one of the most grounding parts of my week, and I like that I get a little stronger and a little more patient each time I show up.

I read a lot, and I love bringing people together. Hosting is one of my favorite things, whether it's a dinner, a game night, or a bigger event where I get to sweat the details so everyone else can relax and enjoy themselves.

And I can't resist playing with data. I'll happily spend a weekend digging through my own training, travel, or whatever else I'm curious about, looking for the story hiding in the numbers. It's the same instinct that draws me to design: noticing patterns, asking why, and making something clear out of something messy.
